root_idea.summary: The root centers on moving or proceeding straight without turning aside; hunting is understood as pursuing and taking quarry in its course.
root_idea.development: The root-level principle is associated with direct, unturning movement. From this, the hunting branch describes pursuing wild game and taking it when captured; related developments include fixed or proud bearing and several specialized lexical extensions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form VIII perfect citation form.
Displayed as the core Quranic noun صَيْدٌ.

senses.definition: To hunt, pursue, capture, or take wild game.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic Form VIII imperative in 5:2; the action is permitted after release from the state of ihram.

senses.definition: Wild game or quarry: an unowned, normally inaccessible animal, bird, or fish that is hunted, captured, or available as prey.
senses.usage_conditions: In the legal Quranic passages 5:1 and 5:94–96, the noun refers especially to game whose taking or eating is regulated; in 5:96 it explicitly includes sea catch. The word can denote either the quarry being pursued or the quarry already taken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In extended usage, to captivate or win people through kindness, beneficence, or good treatment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of the hunting verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the idiom اِقْتَصِدْ تَصِدْ, to aim at what is right and just and thereby obtain what one seeks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed proverbial expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In extended expressions, to draw truffles from the ground as though extracting quarry, or to collect rainwater in vessels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specialized figurative applications of the act of taking or catching.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease of a camel’s head or neck that causes the head to be raised, the neck to twist, or the animal to be unable to turn its face aside.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related vocalization صَيِدٌ is also reported. The condition is associated with a vein between the eyes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fixed or elevated bearing in which the face does not turn aside, especially a proud or haughty posture of a person or king; also an inclination or bending of the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative development from the camel’s diseased posture, not a general restriction on the affected person’s identity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone’s neck to incline or bend.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended causative expression distinct from hunting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make, incite, or induce someone to hunt or seek to capture wild animals, birds, or fish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To afflict a camel with the disease صَيَدٌ, or, in a reported contrary usage, to relieve or cure it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources explicitly report opposite usages for this specialized verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vein between a camel’s eyes, or between its eye and nose, associated with the disease صَيَدٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term of camel medicine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Brass or copper, or a species of that metal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The relational adjective صَادِيٌّ means made of or pertaining to this brass or copper.

other_classical_meanings.definition: White stone used for making cooking pots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized material term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rugged or pebbly ground, including red earth with rough stones, level ground covered with pebbles, or the pebbles themselves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Several closely related geographical applications are reported under this headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Copper, including a gold-like material or glint found in stone cooking pots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The gold-like description concerns the appearance of material in a cooking pot rather than a separate precious-metal sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stone cooking pots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun, with a singulative form reported in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Small pebbles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially in the expression صَيْدَانُ الحَصَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A demon of the kind called غُولٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized folkloric noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman of evil disposition and much talk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source explicitly applies this lexical use to a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who takes, captures, or ensnares something from her husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or idiomatic description reported from traditional usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hunter, fowler, or fisherman; also an animal used for catching game, such as a hunting dog or hawk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intensive form denotes habitual or characteristic practice and can be applied to a female or to a trained hunting animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The shank or lower leg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal usage reported for Yemen, unrelated to the ordinary active-participle sense ‘hunter’.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow that goes straight or hits its mark.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of an arrow’s flight or accuracy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most apt, accustomed, or capable at taking or capturing prey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or intensive adjective, illustrated in a proverbial expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lion, viewed as walking proudly without turning its head aside.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative designation based on the proud or fixed posture associated with صَيَدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where game, birds, or fish are taken; a hunting, fowling, or fishing place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun for the activity or its setting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The uppermost or highest part of a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is reported with an attribution that some lexicographers assign it instead to مَصَدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A device used for hunting: a snare, trap, gin, or net.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The variants مَصْيَدَةٌ, مِصْيَدٌ, and مَصْيَدٌ are reported in the lexical discussion.

cautions: The public verb headword is normalized to the perfect citation form اِصْطَادَ, while the supplied Quran occurrence is an imperative form.
The Mufradat discussion of the isolated Quranic letter ص and the title of Sūrat Ṣād is treated as a homographic issue, not as a lexical meaning of the root صيد.

The Mufradat remarks on ص وَالْقُرْآنِ as an alphabetic letter or surah title, with a possible interpretation from صَادَيْتُ; no corresponding QAC form group or secure direct assignment to the root صيد is supplied.
